evidence.flow: Seller creates a listing (/seller/listings/new -> disclaimer -> save draft -> submit)
evidence.actual: Clicking Next on the Financials step with a valid Asking Price ($250k and $750k, 5 fresh drafts, 2 types, 2 locations) never advances to Step 3 and shows no error. Root cause: listingSchema is a Zod .and() intersection (typeLocationSchema.and(financialsSchema).and(photosDetailsSchema)); handleStepComplete calls methods.trigger(['askingPrice','ttmProfit','reasonForSelling']) but zodResolver cannot field-scope an intersection, so it re-validates the FULL schema including photos.min(1). photos is still [] at step 2, so trigger() returns isValid=false and setStep(3) never runs; FinancialsStep only renders errors.askingPrice, so the failure is silent. The seller listing flow cannot be completed through the UI.
evidence.expected: Valid Asking Price + Next advances to Step 3 (Photos & Details)

findings.proposed_fix: Stop validating a slice of a single Zod intersection per step. Give each step a standalone z.object() and trigger against that, or make the combined schema a plain z.object() with per-step .pick()/superRefine keyed to the current step. Also render a summary of any error on every step so a stuck validation state is never silent.
findings.reproduce: As parker.fellows@hellosugar.salon: /seller/listings/new -> accept disclaimer -> Suite -> pick location -> Next -> enter a positive Asking Price -> Next. UI stays on Financials with no error; network trace shows zero Server Action POSTs when photos:[].

findings.check: Schema changes go through tracked migrations

evidence.detail: drizzle/ has exactly 5 migrations (0000_baseline..0004) and _journal.json matches them (no orphans). But `grep -il 'owner_locations|login_events|listing_views|competitor_alert_log' drizzle/*.sql` returns zero matches — none of these four live tables (added by commits 63de01e/13f4503/5491c6f, all with active app code) have a CREATE TABLE in migration history. Also 0001_boulevard_mapping.sql adds listing_locations.boulevard_location_id/boulevard_mapping_status, but current schema (listings.ts:97-98) defines bq_location_name/data_mapping_status — no migration captures the rename/retype. db:push is absent from vercel.json buildCommand and .github/workflows/ci.yml (confirmed by read). These tables + the rename reached the live DB only via a human running drizzle-kit push, with no migration file recording it. Prod schema drift has occurred and is unauditable.

findings.proposed_fix: Run `npx drizzle-kit generate` to capture current drift (CREATE TABLE for the four tables + column diffs), diff it against the live DB before applying, commit as 0005_*.sql. Ban db:push outside local scratch (fail loudly unless NODE_ENV=development, or remove the script). Add a CI drift detector that fails if `drizzle-kit generate` produces a pending diff against HEAD.
findings.reproduce: grep -il 'owner_locations\|login_events\|listing_views\|competitor_alert_log' drizzle/*.sql (returns nothing); compare drizzle/0001_boulevard_mapping.sql column names to src/db/schema/listings.ts:97-98.

evidence.actual: /admin/listings and /admin/listings/[id] throw 'Minified React error #418 (Text content does not match server-rendered HTML)' — a hydration mismatch — on every load. Root cause: ListingsTable.formatDate() uses Intl.DateTimeFormat with no timeZone, so server (UTC) and client (local) format the same createdAt as different calendar dates. Page renders after the error, but pageerror fires every visit.
evidence.expected: No console/page errors on authenticated routes

findings.proposed_fix: Pass an explicit timeZone to Intl.DateTimeFormat (fixed org TZ or UTC), or format client-only after mount / pass a pre-formatted string from the server so server and client render identical text.
findings.reproduce: Log in as admin, open /admin/listings, check console — React #418 fires on every load.

evidence.detail: Five indexes described in DEBT-010 (listings_status_created_at_idx, listings_seller_id_idx, favorites_listing_id_idx, listing_locations_listing_id_display_order_idx, listing_photos_listing_id_display_order_idx) exist only as TypeScript index() calls; none appear in any committed migration (same root cause as the migrations Blocker), so whether they exist in the live DB is unauditable. Separately, getUnlistedHsLocations still applies its state-scope filter in JS after an uncached, unbounded (no LIMIT) fetch on every /browse render without center+radius — fine now, won't scale.

findings.proposed_fix: Fold the five index migrations into the same reconciliation migration as the migrations Blocker, then verify via pg_indexes against prod. Push the hs-locations state filter into the WHERE clause and add a short-TTL cache (throw-to-empty, don't cache failures).

evidence.detail: The listing EDIT path issues 3 independent sequential DB round-trips: db.update(listings) (actions.ts:45-52 / admin/actions.ts:186-192), then syncListingLocations (its own db.batch scoped to listing_locations, persist.ts:229), then syncListingPhotos (its own db.batch scoped to listing_photos, persist.ts:239). Not one atomic unit — a failure between steps leaves the parent row updated while locations/photos are stale. DEBT-027's atomic-write fix only covers the CREATE path (actions.ts:96, single db.batch), not the more common EDIT path used by saveDraft-with-id and adminUpdateListing.

findings.proposed_fix: Build the parent update as a query object (don't await) and combine with the location + photo delete/inserts into one db.batch([...]), mirroring the create path. Add a test forcing a mid-sequence edit failure that asserts no partial commit.
findings.reproduce: Read actions.ts:45-60 and admin/actions.ts:186-201 (3 awaited DB calls) vs actions.ts:96 (1 db.batch).

evidence.actual: Clicking Save on a listing detail page fires toggleFavorite successfully (a reload shows 'Remove from favorites', DB write succeeded) but the button UI never updates — no toast, label/aria stay 'Add to favorites'. Root cause: FavoriteButtonLarge uses useOptimistic + startTransition but toggleFavorite never calls revalidatePath/revalidateTag, so after the transition settles React re-renders with the stale initialFavorited prop and discards the optimistic flip.
evidence.expected: State-changing action gives immediate persistent confirmation

findings.proposed_fix: Call revalidatePath('/listings/[id]') (or a favorites tag + revalidateTag) inside toggleFavorite, or have the client set confirmed local state from the action's return value instead of the prop.
findings.reproduce: Authed, open an unsaved listing, click Save, wait — button still reads Save; reload — now reads Saved.
